issues.legal_issue: A lawyer facing professional discipline must be given a specific charge identifying the misconduct alleged and a fair opportunity to meet it.
material_facts: The disciplinary committee proceeded to record evidence without framing a specific charge or issues.
The lawyer was not told the precise content of the professional misconduct he had to rebut.
The committee attributed a possible motive to the lawyer based on suspicion, although that motive had not been alleged and he had not been given notice of it.
issues.conclusion: The procedure denied the lawyer a reasonable and fair opportunity to defend himself. The disciplinary order could not stand; the appeal was allowed and the matter was remitted for fresh consideration on the existing evidence, without amendment of the complaint or addition of allegations.
issues.legal_principle: Fairness and natural justice require a specific charge even where the governing statute and rules do not expressly prescribe one. Framing issues, consistently with Rule 8(1) of Part VII of the Bar Council of India Rules, helps identify the contested matters and the evidence each party must address. The Court relied on In re: Shri 'M', an Advocate of the Supreme Court of India, in which charges were framed despite the absence of an express procedural requirement.

rule.if: professional_disciplinary_proceeding and (specific_charge_not_framed or issues_not_framed) and fair_opportunity_denied

predicates.professional_disciplinary_proceeding: A professional body conducted proceedings to determine whether a lawyer had committed misconduct.
predicates.specific_charge_not_framed: The disciplinary body did not identify the precise misconduct alleged against the lawyer in a specific charge.
predicates.issues_not_framed: The disciplinary body did not identify the factual and legal matters in dispute as issues.
predicates.fair_opportunity_denied: The lawyer was not adequately informed of the case he had to meet and consequently lacked a fair opportunity to defend himself.

issues.definition: When professional disciplinary proceedings omit a specific charge or issues and the lawyer is denied a fair opportunity to defend himself, the disciplinary order cannot stand and the matter must be reconsidered.

issues.legal_issue: Professional disciplinary proceedings that can deprive a lawyer of the right to practise are quasi-criminal, and guilt must be established beyond reasonable doubt with the benefit of doubt applied.
material_facts: The proceedings concerned a lawyer who had been suspended from practice for three years.
The disciplinary committee did not show that it had applied the benefit-of-doubt principle or required proof beyond reasonable doubt.
The committee relied on conjecture and suspicion, including a possible motive that had not been alleged.
issues.conclusion: A finding of guilt in such disciplinary proceedings must be based on proof beyond reasonable doubt, not on a preponderance of evidence, conjecture, or suspicion; the benefit of doubt applies. The Court found that the disciplinary committee had not applied these requirements and set aside its order, remitting the matter for reconsideration.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 35 of the Advocates Act, 1961, proceedings that may result in suspension or removal from the roll are quasi-criminal in character. The disciplinary body must apply the benefit of doubt and find guilt only when satisfied beyond reasonable doubt. The Court relied on L.D. Jaisinghani v. Naraindas N. Punjabi, which required evidence leaving no reasonable doubt in a case involving possible disbarment.

predicates.professional_disciplinary_proceeding: A professional body conducted proceedings to determine whether a lawyer had committed misconduct.
predicates.professional_practice_at_risk: The proceeding could result in suspension from practice or removal from the professional roll.

issues.definition: If professional disciplinary proceedings put a lawyer's right to practise at risk, guilt must be proved beyond reasonable doubt and the benefit of doubt must be applied.

issues.legal_issue: A disciplinary finding based on alleged negligence must distinguish simple or tolerable negligence from culpable negligence and assess good faith, motive, and applicable professional standards.
material_facts: The lawyer withdrew a client's suit without written instructions after receiving oral instructions from a person closely connected with the client and involved in bringing the client to the lawyer.
The lawyer maintained that he honestly believed the person was authorised to give instructions on the client's behalf.
Dishonesty or a corrupt motive had not been alleged by the complainant.
The disciplinary committee did not adequately examine the lawyer's bona fides, mens rea, possible negligence, or whether any negligence was culpable.
issues.conclusion: The disciplinary committee was required to assess whether the lawyer acted in good faith and whether any negligence amounted to culpable negligence constituting professional misconduct, having regard to professional standards. The Court did not decide whether the lawyer's conduct was misconduct; it remitted that question for reconsideration.
issues.legal_principle: In assessing alleged professional negligence, the disciplinary body must distinguish tolerable or simple negligence from culpable negligence and consider the lawyer's good faith, mens rea, and professional standards. The Court referred to the standards of professional conduct and etiquette in Chapter II of Part VI of the Bar Council of India Rules, framed under Sections 49(1)(g) and 60(3) of the Advocates Act, 1961.

predicates.professional_disciplinary_proceeding: A professional body conducted proceedings to determine whether a lawyer had committed misconduct.
predicates.negligence_alleged_against_lawyer: The lawyer's conduct was alleged to involve a failure to exercise proper care in professional work.

issues.definition: When negligence is alleged in professional disciplinary proceedings, the misconduct assessment must evaluate culpability, good faith, and professional standards.
